purpose: Test plural African and Africana structures while preserving named language, region, genre, gender, colonial, diasporic, and community authority conditions.

packet_slots.position: Akan personhood, community, moral achievement, sunsum/okra, agency, and responsibility
Yorùbá person, orí, àṣẹ, character, destiny, divination, and epistemic-practical relation
ubuntu/botho relational personhood, dignity, obligation, reconciliation, law, and internal criticism
Zera Yacob and Walda Heywat on inquiry, reason, creator, harmony, moral equality, and textual custody
Du Bois, Césaire, Fanon, Nkrumah, and related Africana inquiry on race, coloniality, double consciousness, liberation, violence, and new humanism
ethnophilosophy dispute, philosophical sagacity, conceptual decolonization, language, professional philosophy, and tradition/modernity critique
African feminist and gender critiques of universal woman, colonial gender systems, personhood, family, power, and epistemic custody
oral, proverbial, narrative, musical, artistic, literary, and political forms as philosophical argument, memory, performance, and public reasoning

selection_rules: African, Sub-Saharan, Black, Africana, Indigenous, traditional, communal, and ubuntu are not synonyms or one civilizational worldview.
Every record retains named language, region, genre, author/community authority, historical setting, and diaspora or colonial relation where known.
Oral performance is neither anonymous raw data nor automatically communal consensus; published reconstruction does not own community meaning.
Feminist, anti-colonial, professional-philosophy, ethnophilosophy, and tradition claims remain internally contested and cannot be token exceptions.
No customary, religious, legal, gender, racial, revolutionary, reconciliatory, or community claim becomes Factorium guidance.
